players.product: High-capacitance (1uF-100uF) X5R/X6S BME MLCCs (GRM/GCM series) for PDN decoupling

quarterly_data.signal: Executive Deputy President Minamide: Q1 (Apr-Jun 2026) revenue was JPY502.3 billion, a record high on a quarterly basis, up 20.7% YoY and up 12.6% excluding foreign exchange effects, driven mainly by data centers and mobility with the components business as the core; operating profit was JPY98.5 billion (not a record), up 59.8% YoY and up 32.6% excluding FX, on operating leverage from higher production volume and yen depreciation.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue JPY502.3 billion (+20.7% YoY, +12.6% ex-FX); operating profit JPY98.5 billion (+59.8% YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: Minamide: full-year forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027 raised - revenue up JPY150 billion from the April forecast to a record JPY2.11 trillion and operating profit up JPY50 billion to a record JPY430 billion, on expanding data-center component demand (mainly AI servers) and a revised FX assumption of JPY155 to the US dollar from Q2 (previously JPY150); the profit raise is held back by rising material costs and higher fixed costs. Capex raised JPY5 billion to JPY255 billion, mainly devices/modules. Data-center-related demand is now seen up just under JPY200 billion versus FY2025, a growth rate of 110%. Q4 revenue is planned above Q3 because major customers' models are now split into fall and spring models.
quarterly_data.figure: FY revenue JPY2.11 trillion (+JPY150 billion); operating profit JPY430 billion (+JPY50 billion); capex JPY255 billion; data-center demand +110%

quarterly_data.signal: Minamide: Q1 orders were very strong, mainly data-center demand; book-to-bill 1.34 times for the total and 1.47 times for MLCCs alone, so strong orders continue. Some longer lead-time orders are also coming in and the take-up rate for Murata components remains firm even as smartphone and automobile set numbers were revised slightly down.

Senior EVP Omori (Ceramic Capacitor Business Unit): MLCC utilization continues very close to 95%; 'what we make is shipped out right away', so inventory is not expected to increase significantly; with a very large number of orders Murata is managing balanced supply against specified delivery dates and is allocating supply while prioritizing customers with ongoing relationships. Minamide: due to tight data-center orders, the H1 inventory increase is now expected to be smaller than the JPY17 billion said in April. Omori: there has not been much capacity conversion - AI data-center (high-capacitance, compact) MLCC capacity is pure incremental; Murata will fully utilize the capacity added each year, improve productivity, and consider additional expansion if that is not enough, discussing the next two to three years carefully; he acknowledged 'there may be a gap versus the pace' of demand.

Data-center growth detail: data-center-related revenue (classified separately under computers from this fiscal year) rose 81% YoY and 24% QoQ in Q1 (Minamide). Omori: AI-data-center capacitor sales grew about 35% to 40% QoQ in real terms, still expecting close to 80% YoY when annualized; the initial 85% to 90% growth plan 'hasn't really changed much' and current orders are 'running a little above that'. Minamide: for the Murata group, data-center sales are expected to grow more than 100% for the full year and data-center MLCCs slightly above 100%; data-center MLCCs rose about 35% to 40% from Q4 to Q1 and 75% to 80% YoY in Q1 (around the high-70% range). The data-center forecast raise is mostly MLCCs, then power supplies, with inductors / EMI filters for data centers and HDD actuators also revised up.
quarterly_data.figure: data-center revenue +81% YoY, +24% QoQ; DC MLCC +75% to 80% YoY in Q1; full-year DC MLCC slightly above 100%

quarterly_data.signal: Pricing (Omori): prices are moving very significantly in many areas, the market's supply portfolio is changing and some price raising is being heard, so 'there may be cases where some adjustments are needed' - e.g. if distortions arise or orders concentrate in certain areas; this is not reflected in the forecast. Some distributor orders (Asia) come in large quantities through market dynamics; for such extra volume Murata will consider a price response, and price is 'one of the options', but the approach is to supply within capacity. Automotive OEM negotiations from this autumn will put the highest priority on long-built trust while seeking a mutually beneficial arrangement on cost and price. LTAs: some cases lead to a contract and some do not. Minamide: Q1 price declines were smaller than a normal year but still a JPY15 billion YoY negative; full-year price reductions are now seen about JPY18 billion more moderate than at the start of the year.
quarterly_data.figure: price decline JPY15 billion YoY in Q1; full-year price reductions about JPY18 billion more moderate

quarterly_data.signal: Segments (Minamide): Components revenue +27.5% YoY in Q1 - capacitors strong in data centers and mobility, inductors / EMI filters up for data centers and mobility (inductors also smartphones); components operating profit JPY113.6 billion vs JPY71.2 billion a year earlier, margin above 30%. Devices/modules revenue +6.2% (high-frequency devices and communications +5% with resin multilayer boards up but high-frequency modules down; energy and power -2.7%); devices/modules operating loss widened from JPY8 billion to JPY12.9 billion. President Nakajima: communications modules remain at a minority share (the larger transmit-side module not yet secured), with a turnaround targeted next year and beyond; devices/modules overall expected to run roughly break-even this year.
quarterly_data.figure: components revenue +27.5% YoY; components OP JPY113.6 billion; devices/modules loss JPY12.9 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Costs: at the start of the year Murata expected Strait of Hormuz-related cost increases of about JPY7 billion for raw materials and about JPY6 billion for energy; that impact has grown by several billion yen and precious-metal and other raw-material prices rose more than expected in April (Minamide), also driving higher outsourcing and production-line labor costs. Q1 also included a JPY4 billion positive from the US tariff refund (net of amounts returned to customers). Demand assumptions: smartphones revised down 1% (low to mid-end models), automobiles slightly down mainly ICE.
quarterly_data.figure: about JPY7 billion raw materials + about JPY6 billion energy (initial); US tariff refund +JPY4 billion

quarterly_data.signal: President Nakajima on hyperscaler investment: 'I guess I should not say bubble, but I think it is getting overheated' - electronic parts are not the bottleneck now; power, data-center hardware and buildings are, so there will be a gap with actual demand, but he does not think total capex will fall much and expects some revisions or delays; Murata tracks indicators such as power-generation turbines and fiber-optic networks to align capacity with actual demand. He sees smartphones / PCs being crowded out mainly via memory (HBM has higher added value), with low-end models staying tough. At a recent customer gathering in Tokyo, MLCC supply had been escalated as a major issue and Murata received many requests. Automotive: with global vehicle volume about 90 million units, strong sales reflect autonomous-driving / SDV demand (inertial sensors) and MLCC / inductor demand for EV and hybrid powertrains; Chinese customers are strong on exports. Omori: automotive and data-center MLCCs use relatively different areas, so automotive supply is not a particular concern.

players.product: vertical power delivery (VPD) modules + intermediate bus converters for AI servers

quarterly_data.signal: Power supply modules: Q1 sales increased for data-center applications, but the initially planned large project dropped (announced in April) caused about JPY3 billion of losses in Q1 (Minamide). FY2026 projects are progressing smoothly and the power-supply-business sales increase versus FY2025 is now factored at JPY38 billion versus the initial JPY25 billion, mostly data-center related. President Nakajima: the next project has started production but will not contribute to sales until H2, so power supplies will be around break-even or slightly below this year; power supply modules for data centers and batteries for battery backup units are moving in a positive direction in profit and loss.
quarterly_data.figure: power supply sales +JPY38 billion vs FY2025 (initial JPY25 billion); about JPY3 billion Q1 loss from the dropped project
